body.p: After (perf-7). The same profile puts 12.9 % in sxml_regex_matcher_scan under fn:replace. SchXslt's patterns have the shape (\W*)\$name(\W*): they can match the empty string before a $, so perf-7's start filter skips nothing and every position is attempted, though no match exists unless the literal $name occurs.

item.p: Mechanism: at compile time, find a literal that every match must contain (a required literal, as other engines keep a "required character" or "must-have string"); at search time, find its next occurrence first and attempt only start positions from which a match could reach it, and give up at once when it does not occur. One mechanism for matches, replace, tokenize, analyze-string and fn:regex's functions; errors, step limits and step counts as settled (a skipped position counts one step).
Owns: src/regex.c, src/regex_internal.h, src/function_library_regex.c, tests/regex_test.c, tests/bench/regex-*.xq.

Done when: each change measured before and after (instructions and seconds) in a D-record and the commit messages, with SchXslt's expand stage; the QT4 XP40 and XQ40 regex sets and the XT40 regex sets unchanged case by case, and a random comparison of fn:analyze-string before and after as perf-7 did. Done 2026-10-28 (): a required literal per compiled regex (the longest CODEPOINT run every way to MATCH passes through) and the read set of what precedes it; the scan finds the literal first and skips the positions that cannot reach it, all of them when it does not occur. SchXslt's expand stage 75.3 to 65.8 x 10^9 instructions; regex-literal.xq 0.458 to 0.186 s; regex sets and 18,000 random regexes unchanged.
